mission.title: strimzi: Optimize example configurations of exported metrics against our dashboards and alerts
mission.description: Optimize example configurations of exported metrics against our dashboards and alerts. Requested by 6+ users.

steps.title: Check current strimzi deployment
steps.description:
Verify your strimzi version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n strimzi -l app.kubernetes.io/name=strimzi
helm list -n strimzi 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working strimzi installation.

steps.title: Review strimzi configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant strimzi configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n strimzi -l app.kubernetes.io/name=strimzi
kubectl get configmap -n strimzi -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=strimzi
```
Today, Strimzi provides the following examples for monitoring:
* Example configurations of the Metric exports for Prometheus
* Example Grafana dashboards 
* Example alerts

We call these examples because:
* They are not the only way how to do them

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n strimzi -l app.kubernetes.io/name=strimzi
kubectl get events -n strimzi --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "Optimize example configurations of exported metrics against…" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
Bascially, we have the following two things:
1. The [Grafana Dashabords](https://github.com/strimzi/strimzi-kafka-operator/tree/main/packaging/examples/metrics/grafana-dashboards) and some [sample Alert Manager rules](https://github.com/strimzi/strimzi-kafka-operator/blob/main/packaging/examples/metrics/prometheus-install/prometheus-rules.yaml) that use various Prometheus metrics
2.
codeSnippets:

jvm_memory_used_bytes

kafka_server_brokertopicmetrics_totalfetchrequests_total
kafka_server_brokertopicmetrics_totalproducerequests_total
kafka_server_kafkareque

# Keep only connection-count from socket-server-metrics
- pattern: kafka.server<type=socket-server-metrics, listener=(.+), networkProcessor=(.+)><>connection-count
  name: kafka_server_socket_server_metrics_connection_count
  type: GAUGE
  labels:
    listener: "$1"
    networkProcessor: "$2"
# Keep only raft-channel attributes used by the KRaft dashboard
- pattern: "kafka.server<type=raft-channel-metrics><>(incoming-byte-total|outgoing-byte-total|request-total|response-total):"
  name: kafka_server_raftchannelmetrics_$1
  type: COUNTER
